hero.headline: Friday.
hero.description: Your desktop AI copilot for everyday tasks. Chat in plain language and Friday can read and write files, search the web, generate images, transcribe your voice, speak back, run on a schedule, and connect to the tools you already use.

demoSuggestions.question: Summarize my Discord mentions
demoSuggestions.answer: You have 4 direct mentions across 2 channels. The thread worth your attention is #launch, where Priya is blocked on the API timeout question and tagged you 11 minutes ago.

demoSuggestions.question: Draft a polite decline to Maya
demoSuggestions.answer: Hey Maya, thanks so much for the invite. I cannot make Thursday, but I would love to find another time. Want me to send a few options for next week?

demoSuggestions.question: What did I do yesterday?
demoSuggestions.answer: You spent the morning on the Friday landing page, shipped a small product update after lunch, and closed the laptop at 18:12.

landingFeatures.title: Chat that acts
landingFeatures.description: Ask in plain language and Friday uses tools to finish the job — reads files, drafts documents, searches the web, runs commands, and generates images.

landingFeatures.title: Local and private
landingFeatures.description: Friday is a desktop app. Your keys, settings, credentials, history, and files stay on your machine, not inside a website chatbot.

landingFeatures.title: Approval before action
landingFeatures.description: Writing files, sending messages, and reaching outside services each need your explicit approval before Friday proceeds.

landingFeatures.title: Speak and listen
landingFeatures.description: Dictate instead of typing, transcribe recordings, and have Friday read replies aloud in the voices you choose.

landingFeatures.title: Skills and MCP
landingFeatures.description: Teach Friday reusable workflows and expose new tools through the Model Context Protocol.

landingFeatures.title: Schedules and checks
landingFeatures.description: Run recurring jobs, daily summaries, and health checks on a schedule, even when you are not actively chatting.

howSteps.label: STEP 01
howSteps.title: Make a request
howSteps.description: Type or dictate what you want. Friday understands the goal, constraints, and expected output, then asks only when something critical is ambiguous.

howSteps.label: STEP 02
howSteps.title: Pick tools
howSteps.description: It chooses the right files, commands, web search, browser, image generation, skill, MCP tool, subagent, or scheduled workflow for the task.

howSteps.label: STEP 03
howSteps.title: Approve and verify
howSteps.description: Sensitive actions pause for confirmation. Friday then checks the result and returns an answer, file, image, scheduled job, or other ready-to-use artifact.

quote.text: Unlike a website chatbot, Friday runs on your machine and works through the providers, credentials, and permissions you choose.

faqs.question: What is Friday?
faqs.answer: Friday is a native desktop AI copilot for everyday tasks. You chat with it in plain language and it can use tools to read and write files, search the web, generate images, transcribe voice, speak back, run scheduled work, and connect to external services.

faqs.question: Does Friday send my data anywhere?
faqs.answer: Friday is local-first. Data leaves your machine only when a task requires an AI provider, channel, MCP server, web request, or hosted service you configured. Provider keys, credentials, settings, memory, and conversation history live locally.

faqs.question: Do I have to use one specific AI provider?
faqs.answer: No. Friday is bring-your-own-AI. Add your own provider keys and choose the provider and model for the assistant, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, image generation, and future media services. OpenAI-compatible endpoints can be configured too.

faqs.question: How does permissioning work?
faqs.answer: Actions that write, delete, publish, send messages, access private data, or touch accounts require explicit approval. Friday shows a confirmation prompt before sensitive work proceeds.

faqs.question: Can Friday work from outside the app?
faqs.answer: Yes. Channels let you talk to Friday from messaging platforms. Telegram is supported today, with per-channel access control and channel secrets. Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, and Email are coming soon.

faqs.question: What can be automated?
faqs.answer: Use the scheduler for recurring assistant jobs such as daily summaries, routine checks, cleanup tasks, and reminders. Health checks can run periodically against a checklist and report only when attention is needed.

faqs.question: Which desktop platforms are supported?
faqs.answer: Friday is built with Electron for Windows, macOS on Intel and Apple Silicon, and Linux. The interface supports English and Italian, with light, dark, and system themes.

faqs.question: Is Friday certified for regulated data?
faqs.answer: Friday does not currently claim a formal regulated-data certification. Review your own AI providers' and connected services' terms for how they handle data you send them.

toolCategories: Read, write, edit, patch, copy, move, delete, inspect, and search local files
Run shell commands and manage longer-running processes
Search the web and fetch current pages or URLs
Drive a managed browser when a page needs real interaction
Create, update, pause, resume, list, and run scheduled jobs
Load reusable skills and run selected skill workflows
Use plugin, MCP, LSP, and client-hosted tools when configured
voiceFeatures: Audio recording from the prompt input
Audio file attachments with preview and duration display
Provider and model selection for transcription
channelSettings: Server URL for server and workspace channels
Direct message policy: allowlist, pairing, open, or deny
Allowed sender lists for direct messages and groups
cronDetails: Next run and last run information
Details page with id, schedule, target, delivery, timestamps, prompt, and payload
heartbeatDetails: Heartbeat runtime enable and pause control
Timing controls with 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, and disable presets
Optional active hours with start, end, and timezone
Last event status, timestamp, duration, channel, reason, and preview
System event input that can be sent immediately or queued for the next heartbeat
privacyNotes: Friday is local-first but can connect to external AI providers, channels, and MCP servers when you configure them.
API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, and credentials are secrets and should not be logged or exposed.
Provider keys are stored locally and only used for provider calls.
Settings, credentials, conversation history, memory, workspace paths, channel IDs, MCP server metadata, local files, and agent data are treated as private.
Users can inspect chat history size and clear conversation history.
Application data and user data folders can be opened from settings.
App settings include theme, language, translucency, menu bar visibility, keep-awake behavior, and microphone control.
Tool and MCP actions that write, delete, publish, send messages, or access private data should pass permission checks.
desktopFeatures: Tray and menu bar support with show, hide, and quit
Theme modes: light, dark, and system
Translucency controls for light and dark themes
Keep computer active toggle for background work
Access to app data and user data folders
Navigation through settings sections and command/search surfaces
Error boundaries, loading states, empty states, and status notices
technicalFoundation: Electron, Node.js, TypeScript, React, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn-style components
Cross-process API contracts under src/shared and src/preload
Provider adapters behind a provider abstraction
Local stores for app settings, cron schedules, skills, apps, channels, memory, and session state
Testing with Jest, Testing Library, and Playwright
